subject: Discrepancy in per-request attribution for Nov invoices
messages:
From: Elena Vega <elena.vega@acme.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: billing@acme.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Unexpected per-request attributions on Nov billing

Hi Kimberly,

We just received our November invoice and noticed a cluster of high-cost entries attributed to 'generation' requests that we believe were actually batched embedding calls. Line items around 2026-11-10 through 2026-11-12 show unusually high token counts for a short set of calls.

Can you provide the raw request attribution (request-id, endpoint, model, tokens_in/tokens_out) for the following ranges?
- 2026-11-10 02:00-08:00 UTC
- 2026-11-11 23:30-23:59 UTC

We suspect either a misclassification between "embedding" and "generation" or a change in our client that caused multiplexing to be billed differently. This is causing a VAT reconciliation problem for our finance team — if the lines are misattributed we need an updated invoice quickly.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Vega
Finance Operations | Acme Corp

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Vega <elena.vega@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 08:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected per-request attributions on Nov billing

Hi Elena — thanks for flagging this. We've pulled an initial extract and attached a small ledger (usage_ledger-202611.csv) plus a short sample of raw request ids for the suspect windows.

Preliminary notes:
- We see a handful of requests that hit the multiplexing proxy (endpoint: /v1/multiplex) during 2026-11-10 and 11. In a couple of cases, the proxy forwarded to both /embeddings and /generate in the same higher-level request; our billing pipeline currently attributes cost by the final downstream operation it counts at the time tokens are measured. That can look like generation when embeddings were also produced as part of the same multi-stage call.
- Last week we deployed a small routing change (2026-11-09) that allows the proxy to shadow additional embedding workers for performance. That change can increase the chance of multi-operation attribution for requests that touch both code paths.

We are not seeing token inflation per se (duplicate counting), but we do see attribution differences depending on which worker finished last. I'll loop in Marissa (billing) to confirm whether those lines should be reclassified for invoicing/VAT purposes.

Action items:
- Marissa will confirm reclassification policy and whether a credit is appropriate.
- Ben will assemble exact request-id -> measured-operation mapping for the two windows you listed (we included a short request-id sample file).

I realize this is painful for your VAT reconciliation; we'll prioritize a clear updated ledger and a proposed invoice correction if warranted.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Billing | Redwood Inference

From: Elena Vega <elena.vega@acme.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: billing@acme.com
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected per-request attributions on Nov billing

Kimberly — appreciate the quick look. A few clarifications from our engineers: the client only calls the multiplex endpoint for batch embedding; we never intentionally trigger text generation during those flows. Examples attached in our request-id list show operations that should be classified as 'embedding' only.

Two asks: 1) if you can provide the request-id -> final operation your billing pipeline used (even if that final op was 'generation') we can cross-check; 2) if reclassification is appropriate, can you separate the corrected lines and reissue the VAT-supporting docs (invoice + VAT breakdown) before Dec 1? Our books close early next month.

Regards,
Elena

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Vega <elena.vega@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 10:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected per-request attributions on Nov billing

Quick summary from billing ops after reviewing the ledger and sample IDs:

- We confirm there was no double-counting of token events (i.e., tokens were measured once per low-level worker). However, because the multiplex proxy can fan out, some high-level requests end up with their cost assigned to whichever downstream worker emitted the final token measurement.
- For customers who need strict functional categorization (embedding vs generation) for VAT/line-item reporting, we can produce an alternate report that assigns attribution using the initiating endpoint (the request that arrived at the proxy) rather than the finishing worker. That will mark the batch embedding calls as embeddings consistently.

Proposed remediation:
1) Produce the "initiating-endpoint" ledger for the two windows and for the full billing period.
2) If the alternate ledger reduces Acme's generation spend by >€500 for the month, we will issue a pro-rated credit and corrected invoice (VAT breakdown adjusted).
3) Work with Acme's finance team to provide the CSV + signed confirmation so their VAT team is satisfied.

Ben — please generate the alternate ledger and include the per-request mapping (request-id, initiating_endpoint, measured_tokens_in, measured_tokens_out, model, timestamp).

Marissa Cole
Billing Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Vega <elena.vega@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2026 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected per-request attributions on Nov billing

Hi Elena — attached is the alternate ledger (we included a short sample inline and the full CSV as an attachment). Summary:

- For the windows you called out, 37 requests were reclassified from generation -> embedding when we assign by initiating endpoint. Net effect: generation token spend decreases by 12,430 tokens (~€420).
- For the entire November billing period the initiating-endpoint view reduces generation spend by ~€1,120 (above our remediation threshold).

Next steps I propose:
- We will draft a corrected invoice showing the adjusted net and VAT lines and email it to Acme before 2026-12-01.
- Please confirm an email acceptance (to comply with audit procedures) once you have reviewed the corrected CSV.

Sample rows (from alternate ledger):
request-20261110-0001, /v1/multiplex (initiator), embedding, 20, 0, embed-large-v2, 2026-11-10T02:12:05Z
request-20261111-0042, /v1/multiplex (initiator), embedding, 512, 0, embed-large-v2, 2026-11-11T23:48:11Z

Attachment stubs: usage_ledger-202611.csv (full alternate ledger), request-id-samples.txt (first 200 ids)

Ben Carter
Senior Billing Engineer | Redwood Inference
